newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metro chief says sales to rise four pct.
newsitem.headline: Metro chief says sales to rise four pct.

text.p: The chief executive of German retailer Metro AG said in a weekend magazine interview that he expected 1996 sales to rise about four percent in 1996 and predicted double-digit growth in textile sales.

Metro chief executive Wolfgang Urban also told Germany's Focus magazine that the retailing group was prepared to receive considerable gains from cost-saving measures after the group was created by the merger of some German retailers.
Metro was created earlier this year after Swiss-based parent company Metro merged retailer Kaufhof AG and ASKO Deutsche Kaufhaus with its other German operations.
Urban told the magazine that Metro's return on sales was also "very good" and that "the chance for a higher return are considerable."

He also said that all Metro stores of more than 7,000 square metres would be transformed into the "Galleria" concept developed by Kaufhof in which speciality retailer goods are presented as individual shops within the department store.
But he could not rule out that some stores within the Metro group would be closed down, saying "a few locations are available for disposal."
